nvitk.gui.core.orientation.napari_dim_order_3d(affine: numpy.ndarray | None, ndim: int = 3) → tuple[int, Ellipsis]¶

Dims order for 3D axial viewing in Napari (matches in-plane layout after Ctrl+T).

axial_dim_order alone yields (S, A, R); Napari’s default display matches (S, R, A) for typical RAS NIfTI — the same result as dims.transpose() once, without calling transpose on load.

nvitk.gui.core.orientation._axes_string_from_layer(layer: Any) → str | None¶

Recover layer’s axis-order string (e.g. "XYZT") from its axis_labels or nvitk metadata; None if unavailable.

nvitk.gui.core.orientation.napari_dim_order(axes: str | None, affine: numpy.ndarray | None, ndim: int) → tuple[int, Ellipsis]¶

Napari dims.order: non-displayed axes first (time), then spatial axes to render.

For XYZT data this yields (T, X, Y, Z) so the time slider drives axis T and the 3D view uses array X, Y, Z (no superior-first shuffle on 4D+).

Voxel/frame resolution for axis_char (X/Y/Z/T/C) from nvitk metadata, or None if not recorded.

nvitk.gui.core.orientation.napari_scale_for_display(shape: tuple[int, Ellipsis], axes: str | None, metadata: dict[str, Any] | None = None) → tuple[float, Ellipsis]¶

Diagonal voxel spacing per array axis (used for 4D+ instead of affine).

nvitk.gui.core.orientation.napari_affine_for_display(affine: numpy.ndarray | None, shape: tuple[int, Ellipsis], axes: str | None, metadata: dict[str, Any] | None = None) → numpy.ndarray | None¶

Affine for Napari display.

For 4D+ volumes, decouple the temporal axis from spatial world coordinates so the time slider spans voxel indices (e.g. 15 phases), not a distorted world extent.

nvitk.gui.core.orientation.prepare_for_napari(data: numpy.ndarray, affine: numpy.ndarray | None, *, axes: str | None = None, metadata: dict[str, Any] | None = None, radiological: bool = True) → tuple[numpy.ndarray, numpy.ndarray | None, tuple[float, Ellipsis] | None]¶

Prepare layer display transforms.

4D+ uses scale only (no affine). Oblique 4DFlow affines couple spatial axes into the temporal world axis and Napari then reports ~60 bogus time steps instead of 15. The file affine is preserved in metadata as affine_source for export.

nvitk.gui.core.orientation._lr_voxel_axis_for_radiological(affine: numpy.ndarray | None, ndim: int) → int | None¶

Voxel axis to flip for radiological in-plane L/R (patient R on screen left).

nvitk.gui.core.orientation._apply_voxel_axis_flip(layer: Any, axis: int) → None¶

Mirror one voxel axis in the viewer by negating that column of the affine.

nvitk.gui.core.orientation.reorient_layer_for_view(layer: Any, target: str) → tuple[str, str | None]¶

Change Napari display to target axis codes (e.g. LAS).

Sign-only changes (R↔L, A↔P, S↔I) mirror the viewer via affine flips without rewriting voxel data. Permutations reorder layer.data and rebuild a display affine so the on-screen layout matches target.

Unlike nvitk.types.Image.orient_to(), this does not preserve world-space coordinates; the goal is a visible left/right (or axis) flip in the viewer.

layer’s nvitk metadata dict, unwrapping the nvitk_metadata sub-key when present.

nvitk.gui.core.orientation.ensure_4d_scale_only_layer(layer: Any) → None¶

Force 4D+ layers to diagonal scale (no oblique file affine).

Oblique 4DFlow affines break the time slider and cause out-of-bounds indices.

nvitk.gui.core.orientation._synchronize_4d_dims(viewer: Any, layer: Any, *, axes_str: str | None, shape: tuple[int, Ellipsis]) → None¶

Force Napari dims range/point from array shape (15 phases, not ~62).

nvitk.gui.core.orientation.configure_viewer_for_layer(viewer: Any, layer: Any, *, radiological: bool = False, configure_dims: bool | None = None) → None¶

Axial-friendly dims for 3D; preserve 4D+ volumes (time/other axes untouched).

Radiological L/R affine flips are off by default so raw images align with label masks opened from the same NIfTI grid (file affine, no extra X mirror).

Set configure_dims=False when adding further layers (e.g. tool outputs) so the user’s ndisplay, axis order, transpose, and camera are left unchanged.
